A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Error Optimization research. All 29 pages of each version, including Appendices A–D, provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables sufficient for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification results in Tables 1 and D.1 and original convergence experiments in Figures 1, 5, and C.1. The explicitly borrowed ResNet-18 SO scores do not negate these original results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original classification and convergence experiments, including the results in Tables 1 and D.1 and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The EO reparameterization, energy objective, error updates, and local weight updates remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–4 and the Appendix A pseudocode retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST/EMNIST-MNIST, FashionMNIST, and CIFAR-10/100. The linear and nonlinear MNIST convergence scenarios, including easy and hard inputs, are also retained.

E2.justification: SO and backpropagation remain the comparators in the corresponding experiments. Newly cited scaling methods are discussed as related work, without being added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: The splits, preprocessing, architectures, losses, metrics, optimization budgets, and hyperparameter settings match across versions, including Appendices C–D. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same precision comparison, linear and nonlinear convergence analyses, loss-function and input-difficulty comparisons, and deep-MLP investigation. Added explanatory citations do not introduce additional analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report classification means and standard deviations over five seeds, retain the same seed information, and show batch medians with interquartile shading in Figure 5. No uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1 and D.1 and the convergence findings remain unchanged. Table 1 adds boldface to the existing VGG-5/MSE CIFAR-100 top-5 backpropagation score, 85.80 ± 0.13; its value and numerical ranking are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.5 corrects the continuous-time limit's left-hand time index from t = 1/λ to t = τ/λ, making it consistent with the stated scaling and the derivation's right-hand side. The binomial formula and Appendix C theorems and proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 modestly refines the novelty claim toward identifying the decay mechanism: the introduction acknowledges concurrent scaling solutions, and Section 3 replaces 'previously unidentified phenomenon' with 'previously unidentified mechanism.' The central EO equivalence, convergence, and performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 qualifies the equilibrium-learning discussion by acknowledging prior findings of improved learning at equilibrium alongside this work's preference for near-backpropagation settings. Other substantive limitations remain unchanged; the discretization explanation newly summarized in Section 3.2 already appeared in v1 Appendix B.5.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware, runtimes, preprocessing instructions, and code-access information are retained. Appendix C.3's added explanation that the 20-layer diagram contains 19 hidden states clarifies information already represented in v1, without disclosing a different architecture.

R1.justification: v2 adds Innocenti et al.'s µPC, Qi et al.'s Training Deep Predictive Coding Networks, and Innocenti et al.'s equilibrium energy-landscape work. It acknowledges earlier observations of energy decay and connects the existing initialization explanation to prior findings, providing a limited but substantive positioning update.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized paragraph and terminology edits, expands the Section 3 subsection headings, clarifies the layer diagram, and adds acknowledgments and funding disclosure. The main narrative and appendix organization remain substantially the same.

P2.justification: Table 1 corrects missing boldface for the retained best VGG-5/MSE CIFAR-100 top-5 score. Appendix material is repaginated, including relocated Tables D.1 and D.9, while the figures, table structures, and overall visual design are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves attribution and novelty framing by acknowledging relevant prior scaling and equilibrium research. The Appendix B.5 correction and Table 1 highlighting fix also improve precision. These are useful, limited improvements; the method, empirical evidence, and substantive limitations remain largely unchanged.
